title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
items.content_text: Gilbert + Tobin, a premier Australian law firm, has fully integrated AI into its legal documentation and research processes to tackle increasing workloads. By automating manual legal tasks, the firm aims to optimize service efficiency and cost structures while maintaining high legal standards.

items.title: Sources: Jensen Huang had an extramarital relationship with Nvidia's VP of healthcare, Kimberly Powell; their relationship has been discussed inside the company (New York Times)
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is allegedly involved in an extramarital affair with Kimberly Powell, the company's VP of healthcare. The relationship has become a subject of discussion within the company, challenging the corporate image of its leadership.

items.title: United won’t let your AI agent book your flight
items.content_text: United Airlines has officially blocked AI agents from finalizing flight bookings on its platform. The company cites concerns over potential privacy breaches, unauthorized transactions, and the inability of AI to fulfill mandatory federal regulatory obligations, such as dangerous goods declarations.

items.title: OKX and ICE's joint venture OKXICE plans to launch a US tokenized stock venue on November 23 and list 70+ assets; 56 of the 62 companies it targeted objected (Scott Patterson/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Crypto's race to grab a slice of the US stock market is picking up speed even as many of the companies whose shares are being targeted for tokenized trading are pushing back.

items.title: AWS releases AWS Emulator, a free tool that simulates 200+ of its services locally, saying AI agents wrote it and its team hasn't written or reviewed any code (Todd Bishop/GeekWire)
items.content_text: AWS has launched AWS Emulator, a local tool simulating over 200 cloud services. The company claims the entire codebase was generated by AI agents without any human intervention in writing or reviewing code, aiming to accelerate local testing workflows.

items.title: Google joins the decision-model wave with Gemini Decision 1, scoring 1,000 questions in a single pass
items.content_text: Google Deepmind is introducing the Gemini Decisions API, an interface built for fast, closed-ended decisions like yes/no questions, multiple choice, and scale-based ratings. The underlying model, Gemini Decision 1, processes up to 1,000 independent questions in a single pass across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs. It scores options directly and returns probabilities with confidence values in 150 to 250 milliseconds. Google says it already uses the API internally for dynamic model routing in

items.title: US corporate AI spending hits a new high in October, but growth slows to 1.65 percent
items.content_text: US corporate AI spending hit a new high in October 2026, but growth was modest. The Ramp AI Index, which tracks AI spending among business customers of financial services provider Ramp, showed a 1.65 percent increase month over month. The heaviest AI users spent somewhat more, according to Ramp. The top one percent of companies by AI spending paid a median of $10,200 per employee per month, up nine percent. items.title: Google launches Gemini Decisions API, powered by its new Gemini Decision 1 model, to return predefined answers with confidence scores, at $0.10/1M input tokens (Google)
items.content_text: Google has launched the Gemini Decisions API, powered by the new Gemini Decision 1 model, designed for fast and probabilistic decision-making. Supporting multimodal inputs across text, image, audio, and video, the API handles up to 1,000 queries in a single pass with confidence scores, targeting use cases like automated routing and content moderation.

items.title: United Airlines says it will prevent personal AI assistants from booking tickets, citing data privacy risks and possible FAA and DOT rule violations (Alison Sider/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: United Airlines has announced it will block personal AI agents from booking tickets to mitigate data privacy risks and avoid compliance issues with FAA and DOT regulations. The carrier intends to cut off third-party AI tools from scraping or manipulating its proprietary booking systems.

items.title: United Airlines says it will prevent personal AI assistants from booking tickets, citing data privacy risks and possible FAA and DOT rule violations (Alison Sider/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: United Airlines has announced it will block personal AI assistants from booking tickets on its platform. The carrier cites severe data privacy risks and potential non-compliance with FAA and DOT regulations as the primary drivers for this restriction.

items.title: Silicon Valley's herd mentality in cozying up to Trump backfired as Democrats may seek retribution, China closes the AI gap, and anti-Big Tech sentiment grows (Nick Clegg/The Atlantic)
items.content_text: Silicon Valley elites face potential retribution from Democrats after aligning with Trump. Meanwhile, they are grappling with China's rapid AI progress and rising domestic anti-Big Tech sentiment, creating a perfect storm for the tech industry.

items.title: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Code verified Signal's cryptographic core in four weeks instead of years
items.content_text: DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, an AI system that automates software security verification. Leveraging Gemini-based agents to write millions of lines of code, the system audited Signal’s encryption protocol in just four weeks—a process that typically takes years.

items.title: IBM announces the Quantum Nighthawk r3, its next-gen processor designed to execute 10,000 quantum operations across 520 qubits to tackle more complex problems (Kyt Dotson/SiliconANGLE)
items.content_text: IBM has announced its next-gen Nighthawk r3 quantum processor designed for high-speed, high-precision complex computing. The company plans to scale this by 2027, linking two r3 chips to achieve 10,000 operations across 1,000+ qubits.

items.title: Sources: self-driving simulation software maker Applied Intuition is in talks to raise at least $1.5B led by General Catalyst at a ~$30B pre-money valuation (Bloomberg)
items.content_text: money, reflecting strong investor appetite for defense and autonomous simulation tech.

items.title: A Startup Wants to Fight AI Bioweapons With AI
items.content_text: Radical Numerics, founded by former Stanford researchers, has launched Omnii Defense, an edge AI model. It enables researchers to identify natural and engineered pathogens using only a laptop and USB gene sequencer, functioning entirely offline to address growing biosecurity concerns.

items.title: What to know about this year’s UN climate talks
items.content_text: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) officially kicked off on November 8 in Antalya, Turkey, co-hosted by Turkey and Australia. Against the backdrop of global energy volatility caused by regional conflicts and the absence of an official US delegation, participants are set to engage in intense negotiations over fossil fuel phase-outs and climate finance.

items.title: Leaked memo: Meta's head of infrastructure and co-head of engineering Santosh Janardhan plans to leave in early 2027; he will be succeeded by Dave Brown (Riley Griffin/Bloomberg)

items.title: Imprint, which helps companies offer co-branded credit cards and manage loyalty programs, raised $130M led by Khosla Ventures at a ~$1.9B valuation (Alex Konrad/Upstarts Media)
items.content_text: Fintech startup Imprint has raised $130 million led by Khosla Ventures, reaching a valuation of approximately $1.9 billion. The company specializes in managing co-branded credit cards and loyalty programs for retailers and airlines, aiming to scale further after hitting 2 million cardholders and $400 million in annual revenue.

items.title: The AO3 Shutdown Is Pitting Fanfic Readers Against Authors
items.content_text: Avery has been writing fan fiction for about six years, now mainly focused on the gay hockey romance Heated Rivalry. items.title: Google’s Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps
items.content_text: Google Labs launched Tabletop, an AI experimental tool that allows users to generate interactive collaborative spaces via natural language prompts. Users can input materials and describe their needs to automatically build custom modules like trackers or planners, which support real-time multi-user collaboration.

items.title: China’s Nvidia Honeypot Isn’t Surprising. Jensen Huang Fell for It Anyway
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been reportedly linked to a former executive of a Singapore-based cloud provider, whom US intelligence agencies flagged as a potential Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia's board has launched an internal investigation to determine if the relationship created security risks and whether the tech mogul was targeted in a sophisticated influence operation.

items.title: Tel Aviv- and SF-based Edelbyte, which is building a data analytics platform optimized for AI agents, emerges from stealth with $70M across Series A and seed (Tim Keary/Forbes)
items.content_text: Edelbyte, based in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, has emerged from stealth with $70 million in combined seed and Series A funding. The company is developing a data analytics platform specifically optimized for AI agents to address the critical need for real-time data processing in automated tasks.

items.title: Helsing built an AI system that prepares targets for weapons systems and says every decision will carry a human name
items.content_text: German defense tech company Helsing has unveiled Clarity, an agent-based software platform that distills sensor data into target recommendations. Helsing promises European control and human oversight. The use of comparable systems in Iran, in Gaza, and in a near-miss involving China shows where those promises break down. items.content_text: AI agents are all the rage, but they’re not quite as capable as their purveyors would have you believe. items.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
items.content_text: Google DeepMind has launched AlphaGenome 2, an AI model designed to decode how DNA mutations affect specific cellular states. By addressing the challenge where identical DNA manifests differently across cell types, the model enables researchers to predict functional consequences of mutations, paving the way for targeted disease treatments.

items.title: Rox, which develops AI agents to automate customer research and outreach, raised a $100M Series B co-led by General Catalyst and March at a $1.3B valuation (Morgan Chittum/Fortune)

The AI sales startup has raised $100 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation, Rox exclusively told Fortune. items.title: Anthropic says AI is eroding Nvidia's CUDA lead, cutting an AMD chip switch from months to three days
items.content_text: Anthropic announced at an investor meeting that it has achieved multi-chip compatibility, porting Claude from Nvidia to AMD GPUs. While historically restricted by the CUDA ecosystem and requiring months of labor, Anthropic utilized proprietary AI tools to complete the migration in just three days.

items.title: After the US midterms, Palantir CEO Alex Karp pivots toward Democrats, describing his philosophy as progressive and acknowledging ICE's enforcement missteps (Politico)
items.content_text: Palantir CEO Alex Karp publicly shifted his political stance, aligning with the Democratic party and labeling himself a 'progressive.' He also acknowledged missteps during the company's past collaboration with ICE, marking a strategic pivot to reshape public perception amid political volatility.

items.title: An analysis of 42 interviews since 2022: after US chip restrictions, Jensen Huang's public rhetoric became more admiring of China and critical of export rules (J.D. Capelouto/Semafor)
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing a board investigation and Congressional scrutiny over his shifting rhetoric on China and alleged personal ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Analysis of his interviews shows a strategic pivot from criticizing China to advocating for global technological integration, fueling debate over corporate loyalty vs. profit.
